Surah al-Ma'idah [Madaniyyah, and its verses are 120; it was revealed after the Conquest (al-Fath)]

﴿O you who have believed, fulfill [your] contracts.﴾ The contracts: the firm covenants that are between you and Allah and between you and the people.

﴿Lawful for you are the animals of grazing livestock﴾: camels, cattle and sheep, for eating after slaughter, ﴿except what is recited to you﴾: its prohibition is mentioned in ﴿Prohibited to you are carrion﴾ and the rest of the verse. So the exception is disjunctive (munqati'), though it may be connected (muttasil), and the prohibition is due to what befalls it of death or the like. ﴿Not permitting hunting while you are in the state of ihram﴾: i.e., while you are muhrimun (in the state of ihram). The word ghayr is in the accusative as a circumstantial state (hal) from the pronoun in lakum.

﴿Indeed, Allah decrees what He wills﴾: of permission and other rulings; there is no objection to Him.

﴿O you who believe, do not violate the sanctity of God's rites﴾, plural of *sha'ira* (rite, sign of God's religion), i.e., its markers, by hunting while in the state of *ihram* (pilgrim's sacred state). ﴿Nor the sacred month﴾ by fighting in it. ﴿Nor the *hady*﴾ (offering animals sent to the Haram), i.e., those animals of livestock sent as offerings to the Sacred Precinct, by interfering with them. ﴿Nor the garlands﴾, plural of *qalada* (garland), which were the things hung around the necks of the offering animals from the trees of the Haram so that they would be safe, i.e., do not interfere with them or with their owners. ﴿Nor﴾ [do you violate the sanctity of] ﴿those who come seeking the Sacred House﴾, intending it, by fighting them. ﴿Seeking bounty﴾, i.e., provision, ﴿from their Lord﴾ through trade, ﴿and approval﴾ from Him, by their intention according to their corrupt assumption. This [prohibition] has been abrogated (*mansukh*) by the verse of Surat Bara'ah (Repentance). ﴿And when you have come out of the state of ihram﴾, ﴿then hunt﴾, an imperative of permission. ﴿And let not hatred of a people﴾, with the *nun* of *shana'an* pronounced with a fatha or with a sukun, meaning enmity, ﴿because they barred you from the Sacred Mosque, drive you to transgress﴾ against them by killing and otherwise. ﴿Cooperate in righteousness﴾ by doing what you have been commanded, ﴿and piety﴾ by abstaining from what you have been forbidden. ﴿And do not cooperate in sin﴾ (*al-ithm*, the acts of disobedience) ﴿and aggression﴾ (*al-'udwan*, transgressing the limits of God). In *wa-la ta'awanu* there is an elision of one of the two *ta'*s in the original (*tatawanu*). ﴿And fear God﴾, i.e., fear His punishment by obeying Him. ﴿Indeed God is severe in punishment﴾ for those who oppose Him.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 5, verse 3:

﴿Forbidden to you is carrion﴾, i.e., its eating, ﴿and blood﴾, i.e., that which is poured forth, as in Surat al-An'am, ﴿and the flesh of swine, and that over which has been invoked [the name] of other than Allah﴾, by being slaughtered in the name of someone other than Him, ﴿and the strangled [animal]﴾, the animal that died by strangulation, ﴿and the beaten [animal]﴾, the one killed by being struck, ﴿and the fallen [animal]﴾, the one that fell from a height to a lower place and died, ﴿and the one gored [to death]﴾, the one killed by the goring of another animal, ﴿and that from which a predator has eaten﴾, ﴿except what you have slaughtered﴾, i.e., what you reached while the soul was still in it from these things, and so you slaughtered it. ﴿And what is sacrificed on﴾ [the name of] ﴿the stone altars﴾, the plural of nisab, which are the idols. ﴿And [it is forbidden] that you seek decision by the arrows﴾, i.e., that you seek apportionment and judgment, ﴿by the arrows﴾, the plural of zalam, with the z vowelled with a fatha and also with a damma, together with a fatha on the l, meaning a small arrow-shaft (qidh, with a kasra on the q) having neither feathers nor head. There were seven of them with the custodian of the Ka'bah, bearing markings, and they would judge by them: if they commanded them, they complied, and if they forbade them, they refrained. ﴿That is defiant disobedience﴾, i.e., departure from obedience. It was revealed on the Day of 'Arafah in the year of the Farewell Pilgrimage: ﴿Today those who disbelieve have despaired of your religion﴾, that you would revert from it, after their hope of that, because of what they saw of its strength. ﴿So do not fear them, but fear Me. Today I have perfected for you your religion﴾, its rulings and obligations, so no lawful or unlawful matter was revealed after it. ﴿And I have completed My favor upon you﴾ by its completion; it was also said, by your entering Makkah in security. ﴿And I have approved﴾, i.e., chosen, ﴿for you Islam as a religion. But whoever is compelled by extreme hunger﴾, starvation, to any of what has been forbidden to him, and eats it, ﴿without inclining toward sin﴾, deviating toward wrongdoing, ﴿then indeed, Allah is Forgiving﴾ of what he ate, ﴿Merciful﴾ toward him in permitting it. This is in contrast to one who inclines toward sin, i.e., one who is engaged in it, such as a highway robber or a rebel, for example, for whom eating is not lawful.

﴿They ask you﴾, O Muhammad, ﴿what has been made lawful for them?﴾ Of food. ﴿Say: The good things have been made lawful for you﴾, meaning the pleasant things, ﴿and [the game caught by] what you have trained of the hunting animals﴾, meaning the predatory ones (al-kawasib) from dogs, beasts of prey, and birds, ﴿training them﴾, a circumstantial clause (hal) from the verb "kallabtu al-kalb" with the doubled letter, meaning I sent the dog out to hunt. ﴿You teach them﴾, a circumstantial clause (hal) from the pronoun in mukallibin, meaning you train them, ﴿in what Allah has taught you﴾, from the etiquettes of hunting. ﴿Then eat of what they catch for you﴾, even if they have killed it, provided they did not eat from it. This is unlike an untrained animal, whose game is not lawful. The sign of training is that it runs off when sent, stops when called back, holds the game, and does not eat from it. The minimum by which it is known is three times. If it eats from the game, then it has not caught it for its owner, and it is not lawful to eat, as in the hadith of the two Sahihs (Bukhari and Muslim). In it is also that game caught by an arrow, when it is shot and the name of Allah is mentioned over it, is like the game of a trained hunting animal. ﴿And mention the name of Allah over it﴾, at the time of releasing it.

This is the commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 5, verse 5:

﴿Today the good things have been made lawful for you﴾, the delicious things, ﴿and the food of those who were given the Scripture﴾, that is, the slaughtered animals of the Jews and the Christians, ﴿is lawful﴾, permitted, ﴿for you, and your food﴾ for them, ﴿is lawful for them. And [lawful for you are] the chaste women﴾, the free women, ﴿from among those who were given the Scripture before you﴾, lawful for you to marry them, ﴿when you have given them their wages﴾, their dowries, ﴿being chaste﴾, married, ﴿not fornicating﴾, openly committing adultery with them, ﴿nor taking them as secret lovers﴾, from among them, secretly committing adultery with them. ﴿And whoever disbelieves in the faith﴾, that is, apostatizes, ﴿his deeds are vain﴾, his good deeds performed before that, so they are not counted nor rewarded, ﴿and in the Hereafter he will be among the losers﴾ if he dies in that state.

Tafsir al-Jalalayn (Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti) on Surah 5, verse 6:

﴿O you who have believed, when you rise to [perform] the prayer﴾, meaning, when you intend to rise, ﴿[while] you are in a state of minor impurity [ḥadath], then wash your faces and your hands to the elbows﴾, meaning, along with them, as the Sunnah (the Prophetic tradition) has clarified. ﴿And wipe over your heads﴾. The *bāʾ* (بِ) here is *lil-ilṣāq* (indicating attachment), meaning, attach the wiping to them without letting water flow. It is a noun of genus (ism jins), so the least that applies to it suffices, which is wiping over part of the hair. This is the view of al-Shāfiʿī. ﴿And your feet﴾, read in the accusative (*naṣb*) as a conjunction (ʿaṭf) with ﴿your hands﴾, and in the genitive (*jarr*) by way of *al-jiwār* (adjacency). ﴿To the ankles﴾, meaning, along with them, as the Sunnah has clarified. The ankles (*al-kaʿbān*) are the two protruding bones on each foot at the joint of the leg and the foot. The separation of the hands and feet (which are washed) from the head (which is wiped) indicates the obligation of *tartīb* (sequence) in the purification of these limbs. This is the view of al-Shāfiʿī. From the Sunnah is derived the obligation of intention (*niyyah*) in it, as in other acts of worship. ﴿And if you are in a state of major impurity [junub], then purify yourselves﴾, meaning, then bathe. ﴿And if you are ill﴾, with an illness that water would harm, ﴿or on a journey﴾, meaning, travelling, ﴿or one of you comes from the place of relieving oneself [al-ghāʾiṭ]﴾, meaning, has passed wind, ﴿or you have touched women﴾, the same has been mentioned before in the verse of women. ﴿And you find no water﴾ after seeking it, ﴿then perform tayammum, intend﴾, ﴿clean earth﴾, meaning, pure soil, ﴿and wipe over your faces and your hands﴾, along with the two elbows, ﴿with it﴾, by two strikes. The *bāʾ* is *lil-ilṣāq*, and the Sunnah has clarified that what is meant is covering both limbs with the wiping. ﴿Allah does not intend to make for you any hardship﴾, meaning, constriction, through what He has obligated upon you of ablution, bathing and tayammum, ﴿but He intends to purify you﴾, from minor and major impurities and sins, ﴿and to complete His favour upon you﴾, by Islam, through clarifying the laws of the religion, ﴿that you may be grateful﴾ for His blessings.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 5, verse 7:

﴿And remember the favour of Allah upon you﴾ by (guiding you to) Islam, ﴿and His covenant﴾ His pledge ﴿with which He bound you﴾ He made a covenant with you concerning it ﴿when you said﴾ to the Prophet (ﷺ) when you pledged allegiance to him, ﴿"We hear and we obey"﴾ in everything you command and forbid, whether it is what you love or what you dislike; ﴿and fear Allah﴾ regarding His covenant, that you should break it. ﴿Indeed, Allah is Knowing of what is within the breasts﴾ of what is in the hearts, so how much more so (is He aware of) other than that.

Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 5, verse 8:

﴿O you who have believed, be steadfast﴾ standing (قائِمِينَ) ﴿for Allah﴾ in discharging His rights, ﴿witnesses in justice﴾ with equity (بِالعَدْلِ). ﴿And do not let the hatred of a people﴾ carry you (يَحْمِلَنكُمْ) ﴿and hatred (بُغْض)﴾ of a people, meaning the disbelievers, ﴿to refrain from being just﴾ so that you wrong them because of their enmity. ﴿Be just﴾ toward the enemy and toward the friend. ﴿That﴾ meaning justice ﴿is nearer to righteousness﴾ and ﴿fear Allah. Indeed, Allah is Acquainted with what you do﴾, so He will reward you for it.
﴿Allah has promised those who believe and do righteous deeds﴾ a good promise, ﴿for them is forgiveness and a great reward﴾, which is the Garden (Paradise).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 5, verse 11:

﴿O you who have believed, remember the favour of Allah upon you when a people determined to extend their hands against you, but He restrained their hands from you⦾﴾ (they were the Quraysh) ﴿to extend﴾ (to stretch out) ﴿their hands to you﴾ (to strike you) ﴿to treacherously harm you﴾, ﴿but He restrained their hands from you﴾ and protected you from what they intended for you.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 5, verse 12:

﴿And Allah had certainly taken the covenant of the Children of Israel﴾ concerning what is mentioned after it. ﴿And We raised up﴾ — here there is a shift (iltifat) from the third person (ghayba) — ﴿from among them twelve leaders﴾, one leader from each tribe, who would stand as a guarantor (kafil) over his people for fulfilling the covenant, as a measure of assurance over them. ﴿And Allah said﴾ to them, ﴿"Indeed I am with you"﴾ by way of help and support. ﴿"If﴾ — the lam here is the lam of oath (lam qasam) — ﴿you establish the prayer, give the zakat, believe in My messengers, honour them﴾ (ʿazzartumūhum), meaning support them, ﴿and lend Allah a goodly loan﴾ by spending in His cause, ﴿I will surely remove from you your misdeeds and will surely admit you into gardens beneath which rivers flow. But whoever disbelieves after that﴾ — after the covenant — ﴿among you, he has certainly strayed from the even way﴾, meaning he has erred from the path of truth; and "sawa'" (the even/middle) originally means the middle. ﴿So they broke their covenant﴾.

﴿So for their breaking of their covenant﴾ *ma* is extra (*ziyada*, a superfluous particle). ﴿We cursed them﴾ we removed them far from Our mercy. ﴿And We made their hearts hard﴾ not soft to accept faith. ﴿They distort the words﴾ that are in the Torah concerning the description of Muhammad ﷺ and other things ﴿from their places﴾ which God had placed them in; i.e., they alter them. ﴿And they have forgotten﴾ they abandoned ﴿a portion﴾ a share ﴿of what they were reminded﴾ they were commanded ﴿of﴾ in the Torah, concerning following Muhammad. ﴿And you will not cease to discover﴾ this is addressed to the Prophet ﷺ; ﴿discover﴾ appear ﴿of them some treachery﴾ i.e., treachery ﴿from them﴾ by breaking the covenant and other things ﴿except a few of them﴾ those who embraced Islam. ﴿So pardon them and overlook﴾ indeed God loves the good-doers. ﴿And this is abrogated (*mansukh*, i.e., superseded by a later ruling through *naskh*, abrogation) by the verse of the sword (*ayat al-sayf*, the verses of fighting that replaced it)﴾.

And among those who say, "We are Christians," We took their covenant, just as We took the covenant of the Children of Israel, the Jews. ﴿But they forgot a portion of what they had been reminded of﴾ in the Gospel, concerning faith and other things, and they broke the covenant. ﴿So We stirred up among them enmity and hatred﴾ — We cast it — ﴿until the Day of Resurrection﴾ — through their division and their differing desires, so that each sect denounces the others as unbelievers. ﴿And Allah will inform them﴾ in the Hereafter ﴿of what they used to do﴾, so He will recompense them for it.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 5, verse 15:

﴿O People of the Scripture﴾ — the Jews and the Christians — ﴿there has certainly come to you Our Messenger﴾ — Muhammad — ﴿making clear to you much of what you used to conceal﴾ — you were hiding — ﴿of the Scripture﴾ — the Torah and the Gospel — such as the verse of stoning and its description. ﴿And pardoning much﴾ — of that — so he does not make it clear when there is no benefit in it, except to expose you. ﴿There has certainly come to you from Allah a light﴾ — this is the Prophet ﷺ — ﴿and a Book﴾ — the Qur'an — ﴿clear﴾ — manifest and evident.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 5, verse 16:

﴿Through it﴾ i.e., through the Book, ﴿Allah guides﴾ ﴿whoever follows His pleasure﴾ by believing, ﴿to the ways of peace﴾ the paths of safety, ﴿and brings them out of the darknesses﴾ disbelief, ﴿into the light﴾ faith, ﴿by His permission﴾ by His will, ﴿and guides them to a straight path﴾ the religion of Islam.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 5, verse 17:

﴿Certainly they have disbelieved who say, "Indeed, Allah is the Messiah, the son of Mary."﴾ [They are disbelievers] in that they made him a god, and they are the Ya'qubiyyah (Ya'qubiyyah), a sect of the Christians.

﴿Say, "Then who could prevent﴾ (yamliku, i.e., who could repel) ﴿from﴾ the punishment of ﴿Allah anything, if He had intended to destroy the Messiah, the son of Mary, and his mother and everyone on the earth entirely?"﴾ (i.e., no one has the power to do that; and if the Messiah were a god, he would have been able to do so).

﴿And to Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth and whatever is between them. He creates what He wills, and Allah is over all things competent﴾ (shā'ahu, i.e., willed it).

﴿And the Jews and the Christians said﴾, i.e., each of them, ﴿"We are the children of God and His beloved"﴾, i.e., like His children in nearness and rank, and He is like our Father in mercy and compassion. ﴿Say﴾ to them, O Muhammad, ﴿"Then why does He punish you for your sins?"﴾ if you are truthful in that. A father does not punish his child, nor does a beloved punish his beloved. But He has punished you, so you are liars. ﴿Rather, you are human beings from among those﴾, i.e., from among the humans ﴿He has created﴾. You have what they have, and you have what is upon them. ﴿He forgives whom He wills﴾, i.e., forgiveness for him, ﴿and punishes whom He wills﴾, i.e., punishment for him, and there is no objection to Him. ﴿To God belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth and what is between them, and to Him is the final return﴾, i.e., the return.

**Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on Surah 5, verse 19:**

﴿O People of the Scripture, there has come to you Our Messenger﴾ Muhammad ﴿making clear to you﴾ the laws of the religion ﴿after a interval﴾ (fatra, a gap of no messengers) ﴿of [no] messengers﴾, since there was no messenger between him and ʿIsā, and the duration of that was five hundred and sixty-nine years, lest ﴿you say﴾ when you are punished, ﴿"No bearer of good tidings or warner has come to us."﴾ The word *min* in *mā jāʾanā min* is extra (ziyāda, an additional particle with no grammatical function). ﴿Indeed, there has come to you a bearer of good tidings and a warner.﴾ So you have no excuse then. ﴿And Allah is over all things Competent.﴾ Among that is punishing you if you do not follow him.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 5, verse 20:

﴿And﴾ mention ﴿when Moses said to his people: "O my people, remember the favour of Allah upon you when He appointed among you﴾ i.e., from among you ﴿prophets and made you kings﴾ possessors of servants and retinues ﴿and gave you what He had not given anyone else in the worlds﴾ such as the manna and the quails, the splitting of the sea, and other things besides that."

﴿O my people, enter the holy land﴾ the purified one, ﴿which God has prescribed for you﴾. He commanded you to enter it, and it is al-Sham (Greater Syria). ﴿And do not turn back on your heels﴾ do not flee in fear of the enemy, ﴿for you will turn about as losers﴾ in your endeavour.

"They said, 'O Moses, indeed in it are a people of giants (jabbarin), remnants of 'Ad, tall and possessed of strength; and indeed we will never enter it until they leave it. So if they leave it, then indeed we will enter.'"

Said to them ﴿two men from among those who feared﴾ (i.e., feared to disobey God's command), and they were Yusha' and Kaleb, two of the chiefs (nuqaba') whom Musa had sent to investigate the condition of the giants (jaba briyya). ﴿On whom God had bestowed favour﴾ with protection from sin (al-'isma). So they concealed what they had observed of their condition, except from Musa, unlike the rest of the chiefs, who spread it abroad, and so they became cowardly. ﴿Enter upon them through the gate﴾ — the gate of the town — ﴿and do not fear them, for they are bodies without hearts.﴾ ﴿When you have entered it, you will surely be victorious﴾ — the two said this out of certainty in God's help and the fulfilment of His promise.

﴿They said, "O Moses, we will never enter it as long as they remain in it. So go, you and your Lord, and fight. Indeed, we are sitting right here."﴾ They [said] ﴿Indeed, we are sitting right here﴾ from fighting.

Musa said, at that time: ﴿O my Lord, I possess none but myself and my brother﴾, meaning, I do not possess anyone else, so that I could compel them to obey. ﴿So part [us] from﴾ them, that is, ﴿separate﴾ us from them.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 5, verse 26:

﴿He said﴾ (God Most High said to him), ﴿"Then it shall be forbidden to them﴾ (i.e., the Holy Land) ﴿for forty years, during which they will wander bewildered﴾ (yatīhūna, i.e., they will be perplexed) ﴿in the land﴾, which measures nine farsakhs, as related by Ibn ʿAbbās. ﴿So do not grieve﴾ (ta's, i.e., do not be sad) ﴿over the defiant people.﴾" It is narrated that they used to travel by night, heading in a direction, but when they woke in the morning they found themselves at the place from which they had set out; and they would travel by day in the same way, until they all died out, except those who had not yet reached twenty years of age. It was said: they numbered six hundred thousand. Hārūn and Mūsā died during the wandering (tīh), and it was a mercy for the two of them and a punishment for those others. When Mūsā was dying, he asked his Lord to bring him near the Holy Land, a stone's throw away, and He brought him near, as is mentioned in the hadith. Yūshaʿ (Joshua) was made a prophet after the forty years and was commanded to fight the giants (al-jabbārīn); so he set out with those who remained with him and fought them. That was on a Friday, and the sun stood still for him for an hour until he finished fighting them. Aḥmad related in his Musnad the hadith: "The sun was not held back for any human except for Yūshaʿ, on the nights he traveled to Bayt al-Maqdis."

Tafsir al-Jalalayn (al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti) on Surah 5, verse 27:

﴿And recite﴾ O Muhammad, ﴿to them﴾, to your people, ﴿the account﴾ the news ﴿of the two sons of Adam﴾, Habil and Qabil, ﴿in truth﴾. The phrase "in truth" is connected to "recite".

﴿When they both offered a sacrifice﴾ to Allah, and it was a ram for Habil and a crop for Qabil, ﴿and it was accepted from one of them﴾, who was Habil, in that a fire came down from the sky and consumed his offering, ﴿and it was not accepted from the other﴾, who was Qabil. So he became angry and concealed envy in his soul until Adam performed the pilgrimage. ﴿He said﴾ to him: ﴿"I will surely kill you."﴾ He said: "Why?" He replied: "Because your offering was accepted over mine."

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 5, verse 28:

﴿La-in﴾ (the lam is a lam of oath) ﴿basaṭta﴾ (extended) ﴿ilayya yadaka li-taqtulanī﴾ (your hand toward me, to kill me) ﴿mā anā bibāsiṭin yadiya ilayka li-aqtulaka innī akhāfu Allāh rabb al-ʿālamīn﴾ (I will not extend my hand toward you to kill you; indeed I fear God, Lord of the worlds) in killing you.

Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (*Tafsir al-Jalalayn*) on Surah 5, verse 29:

﴿Indeed, I wish that you should bear﴾ i.e., return ﴿with my sin﴾, meaning the sin of my killing you, ﴿and your sin﴾, which you committed before ﴿so that you will be among the companions of the Fire﴾. And I do not wish to bear your sin if I kill you, so that I would be among them. God Most High said: ﴿And that is the recompense of the wrongdoers﴾.

﴿So his soul made the killing of his brother seem good to him⦄ — it made it attractive (زَيَّنَتْ) to him — ﴿so he killed him, and so he became﴾ — i.e., became — ﴿among the losers﴾ by killing him. And he did not know what to do with him, because he was the first dead person on the face of the earth from among the children of Adam, so he carried him on his back.

Tafsir al-Jalalayn (al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti) on Surah 5, verse 31:

﴿Then Allah sent a crow scratching in the earth﴾ digging up the soil with its beak and its feet and stirring it over a dead crow until it covered it, ﴿to show him how to conceal﴾ to hide ﴿the corpse of his brother.﴾ The carcass ﴿He said, "Woe to me! Am I unable﴾ to ﴿be like this crow and conceal the corpse of my brother?" And he became ﴾ among the ones who regret﴿ over carrying him, and he dug for him and covered him.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 5, verse 32:

﴿Because of that﴾ — that which Qabil (Cain) did — ﴿We prescribed for the Children of Israel that﴾ — i.e., the matter — ﴿whoever kills a soul, unless it be for a soul [which he has killed], or for corruption [done] in the land﴾ — such as disbelief, fornication, highway robbery, or the like — ﴿it is as if he had slain all mankind. And whoever saves one﴾ — by refraining from killing it — ﴿it is as if he had saved all mankind.﴾ Ibn ʿAbbas said: [this is] in terms of the violation of its sanctity and the preservation of it. ﴿And certainly there came to them﴾ — i.e., the Children of Israel — ﴿Our messengers with clear proofs﴾ — the miracles — ﴿Yet even after that, many of them in the land are indeed transgressors﴾ — exceeding the limit through disbelief, killing, and other things.

Concerning the People of ʿUrayna: when they came to Medina while they were sick, the Prophet (ﷺ) permitted them to go out to the camels and drink from their urine and milk. When they became well, they killed the Prophet's (ﷺ) shepherd and drove off the camels. ﴿Indeed, the penalty for those who wage war against Allah and His Messenger﴾ by fighting the Muslims, ﴿and strive upon the earth to cause corruption﴾ by highway robbery, ﴿is that they be killed or crucified or have their hands and feet cut off on opposite sides﴾, i.e., their right hands and left feet, ﴿or be exiled from the land﴾. Or, the penalties correspond to the circumstances: killing is for one who killed only; crucifixion is for one who killed and took property; cutting off is for one who took property but did not kill; and exile is for one who only caused fear. This is what Ibn ʿAbbas said, and al-Shafiʿi adopted it. The more correct of his two opinions is that crucifixion lasts three days after killing, and it was said that it is before killing, briefly. What resembles exile in deterrence, such as imprisonment and other things, is joined to exile. ﴿That﴾, the aforementioned penalty, ﴿is a disgrace for them﴾, humiliation, ﴿in this world, and for them in the Hereafter is a great punishment﴾, which is the punishment of the Fire.

Tafsir al-Jalalayn (al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti) on Surah 5, verse 34:

﴿Except for those who repent﴾ among the warriors (al-muharibin) and highway robbers (al-qutta') ﴿before you have power over them. So know that Allah is ever Forgiving﴾ to them for what they committed ﴿and Merciful﴾ to them. He expressed it this way, rather than "so do not punish them," to indicate that what is dropped from him by his repentance is only the hudud (fixed penalties) of Allah, not the rights of human beings (huquq al-adamiyyin). This is what appeared to me, and I have not seen anyone address it. And Allah knows best. So if he has killed and taken property, he is killed and his hand and foot are cut off, but he is not crucified. This is the sounder of al-Shafi'i's two opinions. His repentance after coming under your power does not benefit him at all; this is also the sounder of his two opinions.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 5, verse 35:

﴿O you who have believed, fear Allah⟩ — be wary of His punishment by obeying Him — ﴿and seek the means (al-wasilah) to Him⟩ — seek (uṭlubū) — ﴿that which brings you closer to Him⟩ — of obedience to Him — ﴿and strive (jāhidū) in His cause⟩ — to raise high His religion — ﴿that you may be successful⟩ — that you may win.

Indeed, those who disbelieve, even if (it were established) that they possessed everything on earth and the like of it with it, to ransom themselves with it from the torment of the Day of Resurrection, it would not be accepted from them, and theirs is a painful torment.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 5, verse 37:

﴿Yurīdūna﴾ (they wish) yatamannawna (they long) ﴿an yakhrujū min al-nār﴾ (to come out of the Fire), ﴿wa mā hum bi-khārijīna minhā﴾ ("and they will not be ones who come out of it"), ﴿wa lahum ʿadhābun muqīm﴾ (and for them is a lasting punishment), muqīm (lasting, enduring).

The thief, male and female: "al" in both is a relative particle serving as the subject (mubtada'), and because it resembles a conditional, the fa' ("then") enters its predicate, which is ﴿So cut off their hands﴾, meaning the right hand of each of them from the wrist. The Sunnah clarified that the offence for which the hand is cut off is a quarter of a dinar or more. If he repeats the offence, his left foot is cut off at the ankle joint, then his left hand, then his right foot. After that he is disciplined (yu'azzar) with a lesser punishment. ﴿As recompense﴾ is in the accusative as a verbal noun (masdar). ﴿For what they earned﴾, ﴿as an exemplary punishment﴾, a punishment for them ﴿from Allah. And Allah is Mighty﴾, dominant over His affair, ﴿Wise﴾ in His creation.

Surah 5, verse 39:

﴿But whoever repents after his wrongdoing and makes amends, indeed Allah will turn to him in forgiveness. Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.﴾ [He returns from theft] "and makes amends" [his deeds]. "Indeed, Allah will turn to him" [in forgiveness]. "Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful." By the expression used here, what preceded is meant: his repentance does not cancel the right of the human being (haqq al-adami) to retaliation (al-qat') and the return of the property. Yes, the Sunnah has made clear that if the victim pardons him before the matter is raised to the ruler (al-Imam), the amputation falls away; and this is the view of al-Shafi'i.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 5, verse 40:

﴿Do you not know﴾ The interrogative here is for affirmation (taqrir) ﴿that Allah—to Him belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth; He punishes whom He wills﴾ His punishment ﴿and forgives whom He wills﴾ forgiveness for him ﴿and Allah is over all things competent﴾ among which is punishment and forgiveness.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 5, verse 41:

﴿O Messenger, let not grieve you﴾ the conduct of ﴿those who hasten into disbelief﴾ they fall into it quickly, meaning they make it apparent when they find an opportunity, ﴿from﴾ here "min" is for explanation (lil-bayan), ﴿those who say: "We believe," with their mouths﴾ with their tongues; the phrase "with their mouths" is connected to "say," ﴿but their hearts have not believed﴾ and they are the hypocrites. ﴿And from those who are Jews﴾ a people, ﴿listeners to falsehood﴾ that which their rabbis have fabricated, listening with acceptance, ﴿listeners﴾ to you ﴿for another people﴾ for the sake of another people ﴿who are from the Jews﴾ ﴿who have not come to you﴾ and they are the people of Khaybar, among whom two married persons had committed adultery, and they disliked stoning them, so they sent Qurayzah to ask the Prophet ﷺ about their ruling. ﴿They distort the words﴾ which are in the Torah, such as the verse of stoning, ﴿from their places﴾ where Allah placed them, meaning they change them. ﴿They say﴾ to those who sent them: ﴿If you are given this﴾ the distorted ruling, meaning the flogging which Muhammad has given you as a fatwa, ﴿then take it﴾ accept it; ﴿but if you are not given it﴾ rather he has given you a fatwa contrary to it, ﴿then beware﴾ of accepting it. ﴿And whomever Allah wills to test﴾ to lead astray, ﴿you will not avail him anything from Allah﴾ in averting it. ﴿Those are the ones whose hearts Allah did not will to purify﴾ from disbelief; and had He willed it, it would have been so. ﴿For them in this world is disgrace﴾ humiliation through exposure and the jizyah (poll tax).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 5, verse 42:

﴿Listeners to falsehood, devourers of what is unlawfully gained﴾ with a damma or a sukun on the ḥā' (i.e., the ḥarām), such as bribes. ﴿So if they come to you﴾ to judge between them, ﴿then judge between them or turn away from them.﴾ This choice is abrogated by His saying, exalted is He, ﴿and that you judge between them﴾, the verse, so it is obligatory to judge between them when they bring their dispute to us. This is the more sound of al-Shāfiʿī's two opinions. So if they bring their dispute to us along with a Muslim, it is obligatory by consensus (ijmāʿ) ﴿And if you turn away from them, they cannot harm you at all. And if you judge, then judge between them with justice﴾, with fairness, ﴿Indeed, Allah loves those who act justly﴾, those who are just in judgment, meaning He will reward them.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 5, verse 43:

﴿And how do they make you judge, while they have the Torah, in which is the judgment of Allah﴾ concerning stoning, and this is a rhetorical question of wonder, meaning: they did not intend by this to know the truth, but rather what is easier for them. ﴿Then they turn away﴾ they turn away from your judgment of stoning, which agrees with their own Book, ﴿after that﴾ the seeking of judgment.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 5, verse 44:

﴿Indeed, We sent down the Torah, in which there is guidance﴾ from misguidance, ﴿and light﴾, an explanation of the rulings, ﴿by which the prophets, who submitted [to God], judged﴾ from the Children of Israel, ﴿for those who were Jews, and the rabbis﴾ the scholars among them, ﴿and the rabbis [i.e., the jurists]﴾, ﴿by what﴾ i.e., because of that which ﴿they were entrusted with﴾, i.e., it was deposited with them, meaning God entrusted them with it, ﴿of the Book of God﴾, so that they would not alter it, ﴿and they were witnesses to it﴾ that it is true. ﴿So do not fear the people﴾, O Jews, in making known what you have of the description of Muhammad ﷺ and the stoning and other things, ﴿but fear Me﴾ in concealing it. ﴿And do not exchange My signs﴾ i.e., do not substitute them ﴿for a small price﴾ of the worldly life, which you take in return for concealing them. ﴿And whoever does not judge by what God has sent down, those are the disbelievers﴾ in it.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 5, verse 45:

﴿And We prescribed﴾ (i.e., We made obligatory) ﴿for them therein﴾ (i.e., in the Torah) ﴿that the life﴾ shall be killed ﴿for the life﴾ if it kills it, ﴿and the eye for the eye﴾ shall be gouged out, ﴿and the nose for the nose﴾ shall be slit, ﴿and the ear for the ear﴾ shall be cut off, ﴿and the tooth for the tooth﴾ shall be pulled out. And in one reading, the four are in the nominative (raf'). ﴿And wounds﴾ in both cases ﴿are subject to retaliation﴾ (qisas), i.e., retaliation is taken for them where it is possible, such as for the hand and the foot and the like; and where retaliation is not possible, there is compensation by judgment (hukumah). This ruling, although it was prescribed for them, is confirmed in our law (shar'). ﴿But whoever forgoes it﴾ (i.e., forgoes the retaliation, by allowing himself to be subjected to it) ﴿it is an expiation for him﴾ for what he has suffered. ﴿And whoever does not judge by what Allah has revealed﴾ concerning retaliation and other matters...

**Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on Surah 5, verse 46:**

﴿And We caused to follow﴾ (*waqaffayna*), meaning We sent after, ﴿upon their traces﴾, i.e., the prophets, ﴿Jesus, son of Mary, confirming what was before him﴾, meaning before him, ﴿of the Torah. And We gave him the Gospel, wherein was guidance﴾ from misguidance, ﴿and light﴾, an explanation of the rulings. ﴿And confirming﴾ is a circumstantial clause (*ḥāl*) ﴿for what was before him of the Torah﴾, referring to the rulings contained in it.

And ﴿let the People of the Gospel judge by what Allah has revealed therein﴾ of the rulings. In another reading, "yahkum" is in the accusative (naṣb) with its lam in the genrative... 

Let me correct that: the second reading is "yaḥkama" with a kasra on its lam (liyaḥkama), in the accusative, coordinated (ʿaṭfan) with the object of "ātaynāhu" (the object of "ātaynāhu" being the subject of the preceding clause).

﴿And We have sent down to you﴾, O Muhammad, ﴿the Book﴾, the Qur'an, ﴿in truth﴾. The phrase ﴿in truth﴾ is connected to ﴿We have sent down﴾. ﴿Confirming what is before it﴾, meaning before it, ﴿of the Book﴾, ﴿and a witness over it﴾. Here ﴿the Book﴾ means the books (plural). ﴿So judge between them﴾, between the People of the Book, when they bring their disputes to you, ﴿by what Allah has sent down﴾ to you, ﴿and do not follow their desires﴾ ﴿deviating﴾ ﴿from the truth that has come to you. For each of you﴾, O nations, ﴿We have made a law (shir'ah, the divine law) and a clear path (minhaj, a clear way) in religion, by which you proceed﴾. ﴿Had Allah willed, He would have made you one nation﴾ upon one law, ﴿but﴾ He divided you into sects, ﴿so that He may test you﴾, ﴿in what He has given you﴾ of the differing laws, to see which of you is obedient and which is disobedient. ﴿So race to the good deeds﴾, hasten to them, ﴿to Allah is your return, all of you﴾, by resurrection, ﴿and He will inform you of what you used to differ about﴾ concerning matters of religion, and He will recompense each of you for his deeds.

Here is the translation of the passage from Tafsir al-Jalalayn:

(The particle) لـ ﴿أنْ﴾ (lam with "an") [introduces the purpose]: "that" ﴿they should not tempt you﴾, i.e., lead you astray, ﴿away from some of what God has sent down to you.﴾ ﴿And if they turn away﴾ from the revealed judgment and desire other than it, ﴿then know that God only desires to afflict them﴾ with punishment in this world ﴿for some of their sins﴾ which they have committed, and among them is their turning away; and He will requite them for all of them in the Hereafter.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 5, verse 50:

﴿Do they then seek the judgment of the time of ignorance (al-jahiliyyah)?﴾ With the ya' and the ta' (as two readings), i.e., they seek [it], [seeking] from flattery and inclination, when they turn away? It is a rhetorical question of denunciation. ﴿And who﴾ — meaning, no one — ﴿is better than Allah in judgment for a people﴾ — with those who ﴿are certain﴾ of Him. They are singled out for mention because they are the ones who reflect.

O you who have believed, do not take the Jews and the Christians as allies [﴿awliya'﴾ — meaning you should not befriend them or show them affection], (some of them are allies of others) because of their unity in disbelief. ﴿And whoever among you takes them as allies, then indeed he is one of them﴾ (i.e., one of their number). ﴿Indeed, Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people﴾ by their allegiance to the disbelievers.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 5, verse 52:

﴿So you see those in whose hearts is a disease﴾ weakness of conviction, like ʿAbd Allah ibn Ubayy the hypocrite, ﴿hastening toward them﴾ into their alliance, ﴿saying﴾ making excuses for it, ﴿"We fear that a reversal of fortune may befall us"﴾ a turn of time that revolves against us, through drought or defeat, and that the affair of Muhammad will not be completed, so they will not supply us [with food], ﴿but perhaps Allah will bring the conquest﴾ the victory for His Prophet by making his religion prevail, ﴿or a decision from Him﴾ that will tear away the veil of the hypocrites and expose them, ﴿so they will become, over what they concealed within themselves﴾ of doubt and of allying with the disbelievers, ﴿regretful﴾.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 5, verse 53:

﴿And those who believe will say﴾ — read with the nominative (raf') as a resumed sentence (isti'naf), with or without the conjunction "wa" (and); and read with the accusative (nasb) as a coordination (ʿatf) on "ya'ti" (will bring): ﴿"Are these the ones who swore by Allah, their most solemn oaths,﴾ — that is, the utmost effort of their oaths — ﴿that they are with you?"﴾ — in the religion — ﴿Their deeds have become void,﴾ — invalidated — ﴿their good deeds,﴾ — ﴿and they have become﴾ — they became — ﴿losers﴾ — in this world through disgrace, and in the Hereafter through punishment.

O you who have believed, whoever among you turns back from his religion, ﴿يَرْتَدّ﴾ (yartadd), with *al-fakk* (keeping the two identical letters separate) and *al-idgham* (merging them), ﴿يَرْجِع﴾ (returns) to disbelief. ﴿فَسَوْفَ يَأْتِي اللَّه﴾ ... This is information about what Allah knew would occur, and indeed a group apostatized after the death of the Prophet (ﷺ). ﴿فَسَوْفَ يَأْتِي اللَّه﴾ (then Allah will bring), in their place, ﴿بِقَوْمٍ يُحِبّهُمْ ويُحِبُّونَهُ﴾ (a people whom He loves and who love Him). The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "They are the people of this one," and he pointed to Abu Musa al-Ash'ari. Narrated by al-Hakim in his *Sahih*. ﴿أذِلَّة عَلى المُؤْمِنِينَ﴾ (humble toward the believers), *'āṭifīn* (compassionate), ﴿أعِزَّة عَلى الكافِرِينَ﴾ (stern toward the disbelievers), *ashiddā'* (firm). ﴿يُجاهِدُونَ فِي سَبِيل اللَّه ولا يَخافُونَ لَوْمَة لائِم﴾ (They strive in the way of Allah and do not fear the blame of any blamer), in this the way the hypocrites fear the blame of the disbelievers. ﴿ذَلِكَ فَضْل اللَّه يُؤْتِيه مَن يَشاء واللَّه واسِع﴾ (That is the bounty of Allah; He gives it to whom He wills, and Allah is All-Encompassing), *kathīr al-fadl* (abundant in bounty), ﴿عَلِيم﴾ (All-Knowing) of whoever is deserving of it. It was revealed when Ibn Salam said, "O Messenger of Allah, indeed our people have abandoned us."

﴿Your only ally is Allah, His Messenger, and the believers who establish the prayer and give zakat while bowing﴾, [meaning] humbly submissive, or [meaning] they are praying a voluntary prayer (*tatawwu'*).

Tafsir al-Jalalayn by al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti, on surah 5, verse 56:

﴿And whoever takes as allies Allah and His Messenger and those who believe﴾, [so He helps them and grants them victory], ﴿indeed, the party of Allah, they are the victorious﴾, [because of His granting them victory]. He placed ﴿فَإنَّ حِزْب اللَّه﴾ (*fa-inna ḥizb Allāh*) in the position of ﴿فَإنَّهُمْ﴾ (*fa-innahum*) as an explanation, because they are of His party, i.e., His followers.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 5, verse 57:

﴿O you who have believed, do not take those who have taken your religion as ridicule and amusement from among those who were given the Scripture before you, and [do not take] the disbelievers as allies.﴾ [Taking as ridicule] "mahzu'an bihi" (being mocked at), [and amusement] "min" here is for explanation (lil-bayan), [i.e., "from among"] ﴿those who were given the Scripture before you and the disbelievers﴾, al-mushrikin (the polytheists), read with the genitive (al-jarr) and the accusative (al-nasb) [i.e., "al-kuffari" and "al-kuffara"], ﴿as allies. And fear Allah﴾ by abandoning their alliance ﴿if you are [truly] believers﴾, sincere in your faith.

﴿And﴾ those who, ﴿when you call﴾ (i.e., summon) ﴿to the prayer﴾ with the adhan (the call to prayer), ﴿take it﴾, i.e., the prayer, ﴿as a mockery and a game﴾, by mocking it and laughing at it. ﴿That﴾ taking ﴿is because﴾ i.e., because of the fact that ﴿they are a people who do not understand﴾.

It was revealed when the Jews said to the Prophet (ﷺ): "In which of the messengers do you believe?" He said: ﴿We believe in God, and in what has been revealed to us﴾, and the verse [continues]. When he mentioned Jesus, they said: "We do not know of any religion worse than your religion." ﴿Say: O People of the Book, do you find fault with us﴾, do you disapprove ﴿of us except that we believe in God, and in what has been revealed to us, and what was revealed before﴾, i.e., to the prophets, ﴿and that most of you are defiant transgressors﴾. This is conjoined with "that we believe" — the meaning being: you disapprove of nothing but our faith and your opposition to accepting it, which is expressed by the defiance (fisq) that necessarily results from it, and this is not something that can be disapproved of.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 5, verse 60:

﴿Say: Shall I inform you of something worse than that as requital from Allah?﴾ (Say: Shall I inform you) I will tell you (of something worse than that) of the people (of that) which you disapprove of (as requital) as reward, meaning recompense (from Allah) it is (those whom Allah has cursed) distanced them from His mercy (and with whom He is angry, and of whom He made apes and swine) by transformation (and those who worshipped the Taghut) the Shaytan, by obeying him. The pronoun in "minhum" (of them) is construed in terms of the meaning of "min" (of), while in what precedes it, it is construed in terms of its wording. They are the Jews. In another reading, the "ba'" of "abada" (worshipped) is vowelled with a damma, and its object is what follows it, the plural noun being "'abada" (servants), and it is in the accusative as a conjunction to "al-qiradah" (the apes). ﴿Those are worse in position﴾ is a specification (tamyiz), because their abode is the Fire (and further astray from the right way) the path of truth. The root of "sawa'" is "the middle." Mention of "worse" and "further astray" is in contrast to their statement: "We know of no religion worse than your religion."

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 5, verse 61:

﴿And when they come to you﴾ i.e., the hypocrites among the Jews, ﴿they say, "We believe," and they had entered﴾ to you, qualified by ﴿disbelief, and they had gone out with it﴾ from your presence, qualified by it, and they had not believed. ﴿And Allah knows best what they were concealing﴾ And Allah knows best what they were concealing of hypocrisy.

**Tafsir al-Jalalayn** (a concise commentary by Jalal al-Din al-Mahalli and Jalal al-Din al-Suyuti) on Surah al-Ma'idah (5), verse 62:

﴿And you see many of them﴾ i.e., the Jews, ﴿hastening﴾ falling quickly ﴿into sin﴾ lying ﴿and transgression﴾ injustice ﴿and their consumption of the unlawful﴾ the forbidden, such as bribery ﴿evil is what they used to do﴾ evil is what they used to do, this their deed.

﴿Lawlā﴾ (why do/did not), ﴿yanhāhumu al-rabbāniyyūna wal-aḥbār﴾ (ﷺ ... ) — rendered as: "Why do not the rabbis (al-rabbāniyyūn, the divine scholars) and the rabbis of law (al-aḥbār) among them forbid them from ﴿their saying of sin﴾, that is, the lying, ﴿and their consuming of what is unlawful﴾ (al-suḥt, illicit gain)? ﴿Surely evil is what they have been doing.﴾" And their consuming of what is unlawful, surely evil is what they have been doing: the abandonment of their forbidding.

Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir (exegesis) al-Jalalayn) on surah 5, verse 64:

﴿And the Jews said﴾ when they were constricted because of their denial of the Prophet (ﷺ), after they had been the wealthiest of people: ﴿God's hand is chained﴾, meaning withheld from bestowing provision upon us. They used this as a metaphor for stinginess, exalted is God above that. ﴿Their hands are chained﴾, meaning held back from doing good. ﴿And they were cursed for what they said. Rather, both His hands are outstretched﴾. This is hyperbole (mubalaghah) in describing His generosity, and the dual of "hand" is used to indicate abundance, since the utmost a generous person gives from his wealth is to give with his two hands. ﴿He spends as He wills﴾, expanding or restricting, with no objection to Him. ﴿What has been sent down to you from your Lord will surely increase many of them in transgression and disbelief﴾, meaning the Qur'an, and ﴿in transgression and disbelief﴾ due to their disbelief in it. ﴿And We have cast among them enmity and hatred until the Day of Resurrection﴾, so each group of them opposes the other. ﴿Every time they kindle a fire for war﴾, meaning war against the Prophet (ﷺ), ﴿God extinguishes it﴾, meaning whenever they intended it, He turned them back. ﴿And they strive upon the earth in corruption﴾, meaning acting corruptly through sins. ﴿And God does not love corrupters﴾, meaning He will punish them.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 5, verse 65:

﴿And if the People of the Scripture had believed﴾ in Muhammad (ﷺ) ﴿and feared Allah﴾ from disbelief (al-kufr)

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 5, verse 66:

﴿And if they had truly established the Torah and the Gospel﴾ by acting upon what is in them, and among that is belief in the Prophet (ﷺ), ﴿and what has been revealed to them﴾ from the Books ﴿from their Lord, they would have eaten from above them and from beneath their feet﴾ meaning, He would have expanded provision for them and poured it out from every direction. ﴿Among them is a community﴾ a group ﴿moderate﴾ that acts by it, and they are those who believed in the Prophet (ﷺ), such as ʿAbd Allah ibn Salam and his companions. ﴿But many of them—evil is﴾ what ﴿what﴾ they ﴿are doing﴾ [i.e., evil is what they are doing].

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 5, verse 67:

﴿O Messenger, convey﴾ all of ﴿what has been revealed to you from your Lord﴾, and do not conceal any part of it out of fear that you may be harmed. ﴿And if you do not do so﴾, i.e., if you do not convey all that has been revealed to you, ﴿then you have not conveyed His message﴾, whether in the singular or the plural, because concealing part of it is like concealing all of it. ﴿And Allah will protect you from the people﴾ from their killing you. The Prophet (ﷺ) used to be guarded until this was revealed, whereupon he said: "Disperse, for Allah has protected me." Narrated by al-Hakim.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 5, verse 68:

﴿Say: "O People of the Scripture, you are not upon anything﴾ of the religion that is valid, ﴿until you uphold the Torah and the Gospel and what has been revealed to you from your Lord﴾, by acting upon what is in them, and among that is belief in me. ﴿But that which has been revealed to you from your Lord will surely increase many of them in rebellion and disbelief﴾ — from the Qur'an — ﴿[in] rebellion and disbelief﴾ because of their disbelief in it. ﴿So do not grieve﴾ (taḥzan), ﴿over the disbelieving people﴾ if they do not believe in you; that is, do not be concerned about them.

Tafsir al-Jalalayn (Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti) on Surah 5, verse 69:

﴿Indeed, those who believed, and those who were Jews,﴾ — they are the Jews (hum al-yahud), a subject (mubtada').  ﴿And the Sabians﴾ — a sect of them. ﴿And the Christians﴾ — (this is) a substitution (yubdal) from the subject. ﴿Whoever believed﴾ among them ﴿in God and the Last Day, and did righteous deeds, there shall be no fear for them, nor shall they grieve﴾ — in the Hereafter. This is the predicate (khabar) of the subject, and it indicates the predicate of inna (khabar inna).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 5, verse 70:

﴿Indeed, We took the covenant of the Children of Israel﴾ to believe in Allah and His messengers, ﴿and We sent to them messengers. Every time a messenger came to them﴾ from among them, ﴿with that which their souls did not desire﴾ of the truth, ﴿they denied him﴾, ﴿a group﴾ of them ﴿they denied, and a group﴾ of them ﴿they killed﴾, like Zechariah. The use of the present tense (yaqtuluna) rather than the past (qatalu) is to depict the past situation vividly, for the sake of the rhyme (al-fasila, the rhyming pause at the end of a verse).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 5, verse 71:

﴿And they thought﴾ (ḥasibū) meant they supposed that ﴿there would be no﴾ (an lā takūn) — with the verb in the nominative (bi-l-raf') the "an" is a lightened form (mukhaffafa), and with the accusative (bi-l-naṣb) it is the governing "an" (nāṣiba), meaning: would befall ﴿a trial﴾ (fitna), i.e. a punishment upon them for denying the messengers and killing them. ﴿So they became blind﴾ (faʿammū) to the truth, so they did not see it, ﴿and deaf﴾ (waṣammū) to hearing it. ﴿Then Allah turned to them in forgiveness﴾ when they repented. ﴿Then they became blind and deaf again﴾ (thāniyan), ﴿many of them﴾ (kathīr minhum) being a substitute (badal) for the pronoun. ﴿And Allah is Seeing of what they do﴾, so He will recompense them for it.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 5, verse 72:

﴿Indeed, they have disbelieved who said, "Indeed, Allah is the Messiah, the son of Mary."﴾ The like of this has already passed (the statement was previously explained). ﴿And the Messiah said﴾ to them: ﴿"O Children of Israel, worship Allah, my Lord and your Lord."﴾ So I am a servant and not a god. ﴿Indeed, whoever associates others with Allah﴾ in worship, ﴿then Allah has forbidden him Paradise﴾ He prevented him from entering it. ﴿And his refuge is the Fire. And for the wrongdoers there are not any﴾ (the word "min" here is extra) ﴿helpers﴾ who will protect them ﴿from the punishment of Allah.﴾

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 5, verse 73:

﴿Certainly those have disbelieved who say, "Indeed, Allah is the third of three"﴾ [of gods] ﴿three﴾, meaning, one of them, and the other two being ʿĪsā and his mother, and they are a sect of the Christians. ﴿And there is no god except one God. And if they do not desist from what they say﴾ of the trinity and affirm His oneness, ﴿there will surely afflict those who disbelieve among them a painful punishment﴾, meaning, those who persisted in disbelief, ﴿painful﴾, meaning, causing pain, and it is the Fire.
Will they not repent to God and seek His forgiveness for what they have said? Here the interrogative is one of reproach. And God is Forgiving to whoever repents, Merciful toward him.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 5, verse 75:

﴿Khalat﴾ (passed away) means "madat" (passed on), ﴿from before him the messengers﴿ (ﷺ)... 

Let me translate carefully below.

"﴿Had passed away﴾ means ﴿passed on﴾. ﴿Messengers had passed away before him﴾, so he too passes on like them, and he is not a god as they claimed; for had he been one, he would not have passed away. ﴿And his mother was a truthful woman﴾, an intensive form of truthfulness. ﴿They both used to eat food﴾ like the other people; and whoever is like this cannot be a god, because of his composition, his weakness, and what issues from him of urine and excrement. ﴿Look﴾, marveling, ﴿how We make the signs clear to them﴾ regarding Our oneness. ﴿Then look﴾ ﴿how﴾ ﴿they are turned away﴾, that is, how they are diverted from the truth despite the clear proof."

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 5, verse 76:

﴿Say: Do you worship, besides Allah, that which possesses for you neither harm nor benefit? And Allah is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing.﴾ [Besides Him] i.e., other than Him; [that which possesses for you neither harm nor benefit]; [And Allah is the All-Hearing] of your statements; [the All-Knowing] of your conditions. And the interrogative is for denunciation (inkar).

Say, "O People of the Scripture (ahl al-Kitab), do not exceed the limits (taghluu) in your religion beyond the truth (ghayr al-haqq)," by treating Jesus excessively, either by making him (more than he is) or by elevating him above his rightful station. "And do not follow the desires (ahwa') of a people who had gone astray before (qad dallu min qabl)," through their excess, and they are their predecessors, "and who led many astray (wa-adallu kathiran)" among the people, "and who strayed from the even way (sawa' al-sabil)," meaning from the path of truth. And sawa' originally means the middle (al-wasat).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 5, verse 78:

﴿Those who disbelieved among the Children of Israel were cursed upon the tongue of David﴾ by his supplicating against them, so they were transformed into apes; they were the people of Ayla. ﴿And Jesus, son of Mary﴾ by his supplicating against them, so they were transformed into swine; they were the people of the Table (al-Ma'ida). ﴿That﴾ curse
﴿They used not to forbid one another﴾ i.e., they did not forbid one another ﴿from﴾ repeating ﴿an evil they committed. Wretched indeed was what they used to do﴾, that is, their conduct in this.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 5, verse 80:

﴿You see﴾ O Muhammad ﴿many of them take as allies those who disbelieve﴾ from the people of Makkah, out of enmity toward you ﴿Wretched is what their souls have put forward for them﴾ of deeds for their return (to the Hereafter), which brought upon them ﴿...﴾

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 5, verse 81:

﴿If they had believed in Allah and the Prophet﴾ Muhammad ﴿and in what was sent down to him, they would not have taken them﴾ i.e., the disbelievers ﴿as allies. But many of them are defiantly disobedient﴾ i.e., they have left the scope of faith.

Tafsir al-Jalalayn (al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti) on Surah 5, verse 82:

﴿You will surely find﴾ O Muhammad, ﴿the most intense of people in enmity toward those who believe to be the Jews and those who associate partners [with God]﴾ from the people of Makkah, because of the multiplication of their disbelief, their ignorance, and their immersion in following their desires. ﴿And you will surely find the nearest of them in affection toward those who believe to be those who say, "We are Christians."﴾ That is, the nearness of their affection toward the believers ﴿because﴾ of the fact that ﴿among them are priests (qissisin), scholars, and monks (ruhban), worshippers, and because they are not arrogant﴾ in following the truth as the Jews and the people of Makkah are arrogant. It was revealed concerning the delegation of the Negus who came to him from Abyssinia. The Prophet ﷺ recited Surah Ya-Sin, and they wept and embraced Islam, and they said, "This is very similar to what was revealed to Jesus."

﴿And when they hear what has been revealed to the Messenger﴾ of the Qur'an, ﴿you see their eyes overflowing with tears because of what they have recognized of the truth. They say, "Our Lord, we have believed"﴾ we have affirmed Your Prophet and Your Book, ﴿so write us among the witnesses﴾ the ones brought near through their testifying.

﴿And﴾ they said, in reply to the Jews who reproached them for their Islam: ﴿What is [the matter] with us that we should not believe in God and in what has come to us of the truth﴾, meaning the Qur'an? That is, there is no obstacle preventing us from believing, given that its reasons are present. ﴿And we hope﴾ is coordinated (*'ataf*, grammatical coordination) with "we believe" ﴿that our Lord will admit us along with the righteous people﴾, the believers, into Paradise.

**Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on Surah 5, verse 85:**

﴿So Allah rewarded them for what they said with gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein forever. And that is the recompense of the good-doers.﴾ [For] **the faith** (al-iman)

Revealed when a group of the Companions resolved to observe continuous fasting and night prayer, to abstain from women and perfume, not to eat meat, and not to sleep on beds: ﴿O you who believe, do not forbid the good things that Allah has made lawful for you, and do not transgress﴾, i.e., do not go beyond the command of Allah.

And eat of what Allah has provided for you, lawful and good (ḥalālan ṭayyiban) — the object (mafʿūl), and the prepositional phrase preceding it (al-jārr wa-l-majrūr) is a circumstantial clause (ḥāl) related to it (muta'alliq bihi).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 5, verse 89:

﴿Allah will not hold you accountable for the unintentional oaths in your oaths﴾ — that is, what the tongue utters before intending to swear, such as a person's saying: "No, by Allah," or "Yes, by Allah." ﴿But He will hold you accountable for what you have deliberately sworn﴾ — with the letter ta' lightened and with it doubled (ʿaqqadtum, in the other reading ʿāqadtum) — ﴿the oaths﴾ upon it, by swearing deliberately. ﴿Its expiation﴾ — that is, the expiation of the oath when you break it — ﴿is the feeding of ten needy persons﴾, giving each needy person a mudd, ﴿from the average of what you feed your families﴾ — from it, meaning the most common and usual of it, neither the best nor the worst. ﴿Or clothing them﴾ — with what is called clothing, such as a shirt, a turban, or a wrap. It is not sufficient to give what has been mentioned to one needy person, and al-Shafiʿi held this view. ﴿Or freeing a neck﴾ — that is, freeing a believing slave, as in the expiation for killing and for ẓihār, applying the absolute (muṭlaq) to the restricted (muqayyad). ﴿But whoever does not find﴾ any one of what has been mentioned ﴿then fasting for three days﴾ is his expiation. Its apparent meaning is that consecutiveness is not required, and al-Shafiʿi held this view. ﴿That﴾ mentioned ﴿is the expiation of your oaths when you swear﴾ and break them. ﴿And guard your oaths﴾ — by not breaking them — unless they are for performing a good deed or reconciling between people, as in Surat al-Baqarah. ﴿Thus﴾ — that is, in the same way that what has been mentioned was made clear to you — ﴿Allah makes clear to you His verses, that you may be grateful﴾ — to Him for that.

O you who believe! Intoxicants (al-khamr), gambling (al-maysir), idols (al-ansab), and divining arrows (al-azlam) are only an abomination (rijs) of Satan's handiwork; so avoid it.

Glosses: al-khamr: an intoxicant that clouds the intellect; al-maysir: games of chance; al-ansab: idols; al-azlam: arrows used for seeking decisions (qidah al-istiqsam).

﴿O you who believe! Intoxicants, gambling, idols, and divining arrows are only an abomination, from the handiwork of Satan. So avoid it.﴾

Commentary (Jalalayn):

﴿إنّما الخَمْر﴾ al-khamr: the intoxicant that clouds the intellect (al-muskir alladhi yukhamir al-'aql). ﴿والمَيْسِر﴾ al-maysir: gambling (al-qimar). ﴿والأَنْصاب﴾ al-ansab: idols (al-asnam). ﴿والأَزْلام﴾ al-azlam: the arrows of seeking decision (qidah al-istiqsam). ﴿رِجْس﴾ rijs: foul, loathsome (khabith mustaqdhar). ﴿مِن عَمَل الشَّيْطان﴾ from the work of Satan, who adorns it (alladhi yuzayyinuhu). ﴿فاجْتَنِبُوهُ﴾ so avoid it, i.e., the rijs described as these things; that you not do it.

Verily Satan desires only to cause enmity and hatred to arise among you through wine and gambling ﴿Verily Satan desires only to cause enmity and hatred among you through wine and gambling﴾, when you partake of them, because of the evil and strife that occur in them; ﴿and to bar you﴾ by occupation with them ﴿from the remembrance of God and from the prayer﴾; He singled out the prayer for mention, to glorify it; ﴿will you not then desist﴾ from indulging in them? That is, desist!

Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 5, verse 92:

﴿And obey Allah, and obey the Messenger, and beware﴾ (of) the disobediences, ﴿but if you turn away﴾ from obedience, ﴿then know that upon Our Messenger is only the clear conveyance﴾, the manifest delivery (of the message), ﴿and your reward is upon Us﴾.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 5, verse 93:

﴿There is no blame upon those who believe and do righteous deeds for what they ate﴾ — they consumed wine and gambling (al-maysir) before its prohibition; ﴿when they fear Allah﴾ — from the prohibited things; ﴿and believe and do righteous deeds, then fear Allah and believe﴾ — they remained steadfast in piety and faith; ﴿then fear Allah and do good﴾ — in action; ﴿and Allah loves the doers of good﴾ — meaning, He rewards them.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 5, verse 94:

﴿O you who have believed, Allah will surely test you with something of the game that your hands and your spears can reach﴾ [He will test you] (لَيَخْتَبِرَنكُمْ) ﴿Allah, with something﴾ (بِشَيْءٍ) that He sends to you ﴿of the game that your hands and your spears can reach﴾ (تَنالهُ), i.e., the small of it (الصِّغار مِنهُ) ﴿your hands and your spears﴾, i.e., the large of it (الكِبار مِنهُ). This occurred at al-Hudaybiyah while they were in the state of ihram (مُحْرِمُونَ), so the wild animals and birds would come upon them in their encampments ﴿that Allah may make evident who fears Him unseen﴾ (لِيَعْلَم اللَّه) knowledge of manifestation (عِلْم ظُهُور) ﴿who fears Him unseen﴾ (مَن يَخافهُ بِالغَيْبِ), [the phrase بِالغَيْبِ being] a circumstantial clause (حال), i.e., while absent, not seeing Him, so that he refrains from the game ﴿And whoever transgresses after that﴾ (فَمَن اعْتَدى بَعْد ذَلِكَ), after the prohibition concerning it (النَّهْي عَنْهُ), ﴿by hunting it﴾ (فاصْطادَهُ).

﴿O you who have believed, do not kill game while you are in the state of ihram (ihram: the sacred state entered for hajj or 'umrah)﴾ ﴿and whoever of you kills it intentionally, then a penalty﴾ is read with tanwin (the nunation of the word), and what follows it is in the nominative, meaning: upon him is a penalty (jaza', نَوْ) ﴿equivalent to what he killed from the livestock﴾, meaning its likeness in form. In another reading, jaza' is in the construct form (idafah). ﴿By it shall judge﴾, meaning by the equivalent, ﴿two just men among you﴾ who have the discernment by which they can distinguish which thing most resembles it. Ibn 'Abbas, 'Umar and 'Ali, may Allah be pleased with them, ruled concerning the ostrich that a camel (budnah) is due, and Ibn 'Abbas and Abu 'Ubaydah ruled concerning the wild ass and its wild cow that a cow is due, and Ibn 'Umar and Ibn 'Awf ruled concerning the gazelle that a sheep is due. Ibn 'Abbas, 'Umar and others ruled concerning the pigeon that a sheep is due, because it resembles it in gulping water. ﴿As an offering (hady: an animal sacrificed at the sacred precinct)﴾ is a circumstantial accusative (hal) of jaza'. ﴿Reaching the Ka'bah﴾, meaning it is brought to the sacred precinct (haram), where it is slaughtered and its meat given in charity to its poor. It is not permissible to slaughter it wherever one is. Its accusative case is as an attributive (na't) of what precedes it, even though it is in the construct form, because its construct form is merely verbal and does not confer definiteness. If there is no equivalent in livestock for the game, such as the sparrow or the locust, then he must pay its value. ﴿Or﴾ upon him ﴿an expiation (kaffarah), other than the penalty, which if he finds it is﴾ ﴿feeding the poor﴾, from the staple food of the region, an amount equal in value to the penalty, one mudd (a measure) for each poor person. In another reading, kaffarah is in the construct form with what follows it, and that is for explanation (bayan). ﴿Or﴾ upon him ﴿an equivalent﴾, the like of ﴿that food, fasting﴾, which he fasts for each mudd a day. If he finds it, that is obligatory upon him. ﴿So that he may taste the consequence (wabal: the weight) of his deed﴾ which he committed. ﴿Allah has pardoned what has passed﴾, meaning the killing of game before its prohibition. ﴿And whoever returns to it, Allah will take retribution from him, and Allah is Mighty﴾, dominant over His affair, ﴿Owner of retribution﴾ against whoever disobeys Him. What was mentioned concerning intentional killing is extended to the case of error (khata') in that ruling.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 5, verse 96:

﴿Lawful for you﴾, O people, whether you are lawful (not in ihram) or in ihram (the sacred state of pilgrimage): ﴿the game of the sea﴾ that you may eat. It is that which cannot live except in the sea, like fish, unlike that which lives both in it and on land, like the crab. ﴿And its food﴾ is what it casts up dead. ﴿As an enjoyment﴾, a provision, ﴿for you﴾ to eat, ﴿and for the travelers﴾ among you, who take it as provision. ﴿But forbidden to you is the game of the land﴾, which is the edible wild animals that live on land, that you hunt ﴿as long as you are in ihram﴾. So if a lawful person (not in ihram) hunts it, it is lawful for the one in ihram to eat it, as the sunnah (the prophetic tradition) has clarified.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 5, verse 97:

﴿Allah made the Kaaba, the Sacred House,﴾ the Sacred (al-Muharram), ﴿a means of standing for the people.﴾ By it the affair of their religion is upheld, through the pilgrimage to it, and their worldly affairs are upheld, through the security of whoever enters it, the prohibition of harming it, and the gathering of the fruits of every thing to it. In another reading it is qayyiman without an alif, a verbal noun (masdar) of qama, without a mu'allal (weak-letter) form. ﴿And the Sacred Month﴾ means the sacred months (al-ashhur al-hurum): Dhu al-Qa'dah, Dhu al-Hijjah, al-Muharram and Rajab, a means of standing for them through their security from fighting during them. ﴿And the offerings and the garlands﴾ are a means of standing for them through the security of their owners from being harmed. ﴿That﴾ refers to the aforementioned appointment, ﴿so that you may know that Allah knows whatever is in the heavens and whatever is in the earth, and that Allah is Knower of everything.﴾ His making this appointment for the bringing of benefits to you and the warding off of harms from you before they occur is evidence of His knowledge of what exists and what will exist.
﴿Know that Allah is severe in punishment﴾ toward His enemies, ﴿and that Allah is Forgiving﴾ toward His allies, ﴿Merciful﴾ toward them.

The messenger's duty is only to convey (the message) to you. ﴿Upon the Messenger is only the conveying (of the message).﴾ And Allah knows what you reveal, ﴿and what you conceal﴾ of deeds, ﴿what you show﴾ (i.e., what you display of action) ﴿and what you hide﴾ (i.e., what you keep secret of it), so that He will recompense you for it.

Say: "Not equal are the evil (al-khabith), meaning the unlawful, and the good (al-tayyib), meaning the lawful, even if the abundance of the evil pleases you," that is, delights you. "So be mindful of God," regarding its abandonment, "O people of understanding, that perhaps you may prosper," that is, succeed.

It was revealed when they multiplied their questions to him (ﷺ): ﴿O you who believe, do not ask about things which, if they were made apparent to you, would distress you﴾, i.e., be made manifest to you, ﴿would distress you﴾ because of the hardship in them. ﴿And if you ask about them when the Qur'an is being revealed﴾, during the time of the Prophet (ﷺ), ﴿they will be made apparent to you﴾. The meaning is: if you ask about things during his time, the Qur'an will be revealed disclosing them, and when they are disclosed they will distress you; so do not ask about them. ﴿Allah has pardoned it﴾, i.e., He has pardoned your asking, so do not return to it.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 5, verse 102:

﴿قَدْ سَأَلَها﴾ i.e., the things (al-ashya'), ﴿قَوْم مِن قَبْلكُمْ﴾ a people before you asked their prophets about them, so they were answered with the explanation of their rulings, ﴿ثُمَّ أصْبَحُوا﴾ became, ﴿بِها كافِرِينَ﴾ disbelievers in them, by their abandoning acting upon them.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 5, verse 103:

﴿Allah did not institute﴾ (shara‘a) ﴿any bahirah, sa'ibah, wasilah, or ham﴾, as the people of the Jahiliyyah (the age of ignorance) used to do. Al-Bukhari narrated from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib, who said: The bahirah is the she-camel whose milk is dedicated to the idols (tawaghit), so no one among the people milks her. The sa'ibah is the one they would let loose for their gods, so no load is carried upon her. The wasilah is the female camel that gives birth to a female first, then gives birth to another female after it, with no male between the two; they would let her loose for their idols if one of the two was connected to the other. The ham is the stallion camel that has completed the number of mating services counted for him; when he has finished his mating, they leave him for the idols and exempt him from carrying any load, and they called him the hami. ﴿But those who disbelieve invent lies against Allah﴾ in this and in attributing it to Him, ﴿and most of them do not reason﴾, that this is a fabrication, because they imitated their fathers in it.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 5, verse 104:

﴿And when it is said to them, "Come to what Allah has sent down and to the Messenger,"﴾ i.e., to His ruling, [permitting] what you have prohibited. ﴿They say, "Sufficient for us is what we found our fathers upon,"﴾ meaning: sufficient for us, [in matters] of religion and law. ﴿Even though their fathers knew nothing and were not guided?﴾ meaning: would that suffice them even if their fathers knew nothing and were not guided to the truth? The interrogative [form] is for denunciation (inkar).

O you who have believed, upon you is your own soul (i.e., guard it and attend to its reform). The one who has gone astray cannot harm you once you are guided. It has been said that what is meant is: the one who has gone astray among the People of the Book will not harm you; and it has been said that what is meant is others than them, based on the hadith of Abu Tha'laba al-Khushani: "I asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about it, and he said: 'Enjoin what is good and forbid what is evil, until you see stinginess obeyed, desire followed, the world preferred, and every person of opinion pleased with his own opinion; then (it is) upon you, yourself.'" Related by al-Hakim and others. ﴿To Allah is your return, all of you, and He will inform you of what you used to do﴾, so He will recompense you for it.

Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 5, verse 106:

﴿O you who have believed, let there be [a valid] testimony among you when death approaches one of you at the time of bequest: two just men from among you﴾, that is, its causes (أسبابه, asbabahu), ﴿at the time of bequest﴾. ﴿Two just men from among you﴾: this is a report (خبر, khabar) with the meaning of a command, that is, let two witnesses testify. The attribution of "testimony" (شهادة, shahadah) to "between you" (بينكم, baynakum) is an expansion in usage (على الاتساع, ʿala al-ittisaʿ). "At the time" (حين, hina) is either a substitute (بدل, badal) for "when" (إذا, idha) or an adverbial of time (ظرف, zarf) for "approaches" (حضر, hadara). ﴿Or two others from outside your [community]﴾, that is, outside your religion (ملتكم, millatikum). ﴿If you are travelling (ضربتم, darabtum) in the land and the affliction of death befalls you﴾, that is, you have journeyed (سافرتم, safartum). ﴿You shall detain them﴾, that is, you shall hold them back (تُوقفونهما, tuqifunahuma), this being a qualifier (صفة, sifah) of "two others." ﴿After the prayer﴾, that is, the prayer of ʿasr (العصر, al-ʿasr). ﴿Then they will swear﴾, that is, they will take an oath (يحلفان, yahlifani) ﴿by Allah, if you doubt [them]﴾, that is, if you suspect them concerning it, and they will say: ﴿We will not exchange it﴾, by Allah, ﴿for any price﴾, that is, any compensation (عوضا, ʿiwadan) which we take in its place from the worldly life, by swearing by Him or by bearing false witness for its sake. ﴿Even if it were [one] of near kin﴾, the one for whom the oath is taken or the one in whose favour the testimony is given. ﴿Nor will we conceal the testimony of Allah﴾, which we have been commanded to give. ﴿Indeed, we would then be among the sinners﴾, if we had concealed it.

﴿Then if it becomes known﴾ (uṭṭli‘a): after their oath, it is discovered ﴿that the two have committed a sin﴾ (istaḥaqqā ithman), i.e., they have done something that requires it, such as betrayal or lying in testimony. This is shown by the fact that there were found with them items like those they were accused of, and they claimed that they had bought them from the deceased or that he had bequeathed them to them. ﴿then two others will take their place﴾ in the obligation of the oath upon them, ﴿from among those against whom the bequest was owed﴾, namely the heirs. ﴿The closest ones﴾ (al-awlayān) is a substitution for "two others," meaning the two nearest relatives of the deceased. In another reading (qira'a), the word is al-awwalīn, the plural of awwal (first), either as a descriptive adjective or as a substitution for "those." ﴿They will swear by God﴾ that the testimony of the two witnesses is a betrayal, and they will say: ﴿our testimony is more truthful than theirs﴾, meaning our oath is more truthful than their oath, ﴿and we have not transgressed﴾, meaning we have not exceeded the truth in the oath. ﴿Indeed, we would then be among the wrongdoers.﴾

The meaning is: when a dying person is to have his bequest witnessed, let him have two witnesses from among the people of his religion, or others if he cannot find them due to travel or the like. If the heirs doubt them and claim that they betrayed the trust by taking or handing over something to a person whom they claimed the deceased had bequeathed it to, then the two shall swear (the rest of the verse follows). If the heirs become aware of a sign that disproves the two witnesses, and they claim the one who received the item, then the nearest of the heirs shall swear that the two witnesses are lying, and what the heirs claimed is confirmed. The ruling stands for the two executors (al-wasiyyayn) but is abrogated (mansūkh) for the two witnesses. Likewise, the testimony of non-Muslims is abrogated. The prayer of ‘Asr is observed for the sake of making the oath more solemn. The oath in the verse is restricted to two of the nearest heirs because of the specific incident for which it was revealed. This is what al-Bukhari narrated: a man from Banu Sahm went out with Tamim al-Dari and ‘Adi ibn Badda, meaning that they were both Christians. The Sahmī man died in a land where there was no Muslim. When they returned with his estate, they lost a silver cup decorated with gold. They were brought before the Prophet (ﷺ), and this verse was revealed, and he made them swear. Then the cup was found in Makkah, and they said: "We bought it from Tamim and ‘Adi." Then the second verse was revealed, and two men from the guardians of the Sahmī stood and swore. In the narration of al-Tirmidhi: ‘Amr ibn al-‘As and another man from among them stood and swore, and he was closer to him. In another narration: he fell ill and bequeathed to them, and he instructed them to deliver what he had left to his family. When he died, they took the cup and handed over to his family what remained.

That is the ruling mentioned above, of returning the oaths to the heirs, "is closer" (adna) "to their bringing" (an ya'tū), i.e. the witnesses or the executors (al-awsiyā'), "the testimony in its proper form" (ʿalā wajhihā), the form in which they bore it, without alteration or treachery; "or" it is closer "that they fear that oaths will be returned after their oaths" (an yakhāfū an turadda aymānun ba'da aymānihim), upon the claimant heirs, so that they swear against their treachery and lying and are exposed and made to pay compensation, and so they do not lie. "And fear Allah" (wa-ittaqū Allāh) by abandoning treachery and lying. "And listen" (wa-usmaʿū) to what you are commanded, listening with acceptance (samāʿ qabūl). "And Allah does not guide the defiant people" (Wa-llāhu lā yahdī al-qawm al-fāsiqīn), those who have gone outside His obedience, to the path of good.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 5, verse 109:
