﴿On the Day when Allah gathers the Messengers, He will say: "What was the response you received?"﴾ That is the Day of Resurrection. ﴿Then He will say﴾ to them, rebuking their peoples: ﴿"What was it?"﴾ i.e., what was the response ﴿you received﴾ when you called them to monotheism? ﴿They will say: "We have no knowledge."﴾ of that, ﴿"Verily You, You are the Knower of the unseen."﴾ of what was hidden from the servants, and whose knowledge was lost to them because of the severity of the terror of the Day of Resurrection and their dread. Then they will bear witness against their nations, after they have calmed down.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 5, verse 110:

Remember ﴿when Allah said: "O Jesus, son of Mary, remember My favour upon you and upon your mother"﴾ by thanking her, ﴿when I strengthened you﴾ I empowered you ﴿with the Holy Spirit﴾ Jibril, ﴿speaking to people﴾ a circumstantial clause (ḥāl) from the kāf in "aydtuka" (I strengthened you), ﴿in the cradle﴾ i.e., as a child, ﴿and in maturity﴾. This implies his descent before the Hour, because he was raised up before reaching middle age, as was mentioned in Āl ʿImrān. ﴿And when I taught you the Book, the wisdom, the Torah and the Gospel; and when you shaped from clay as the form of﴾ the likeness of ﴿a bird﴾ and the kāf here is a noun meaning "like," functioning as an object, ﴿by My permission, then you breathed into it and it became a bird by My permission﴾ by My will, ﴿and you healed the blind and the leper by My permission. And when you brought forth the dead﴾ from their graves alive ﴿by My permission. And when I restrained the Children of Israel from you﴾ when they intended to kill you ﴿when you came to them with the clear proofs﴾ the miracles, ﴿but those of them who disbelieved said: "This is nothing but clear magic."﴾ In another reading, "sāḥir" (sorcerer), i.e., Jesus.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 5, verse 111:

﴿And when I inspired the disciples (al-Hawariyyun)﴾ I commanded them through His tongue (i.e., through the tongue of Jesus) ﴿that﴾ i.e., with [the meaning of] ﴿believe in Me and in My Messenger﴾ Jesus, ﴿they said, "We believe"﴾ in both of them.

Remember ﴿when the disciples said: "O Jesus, son of Mary, can your Lord send down to us a table from heaven?"﴾ That is, can He do it? And in another reading, with the letter ta' on top (تَسْتَطِيع, "can you ask your Lord"), and what follows it is in the accusative, meaning: can you ask Him ﴿to send down to us a table from heaven.﴾ Jesus said to them: ﴿Fear God﴾ in demanding signs.

﴿They said: "We wish to eat from it, and that our hearts may be reassured﴾ (by being at rest) ﴿and that we may know﴾ (increase in knowledge) ﴿that you have indeed spoken truthfully to us﴾ (the "that" here is the lightened form, meaning "that you") ﴿...﴾ in claiming prophethood."

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 5, verse 114:

﴿Jesus, son of Mary, said: "O Allah, our Lord, send down to us a table spread with food from the heaven, so that it will be a festival for us, for the first of us and the last of us, and a sign from You. And provide for us, for You are the best of providers."﴾ That is, on the day of its descending, ﴿a festival﴾ we magnify and honour. ﴿For the first of us﴾ is a substitute for "for us," with the preposition repeated. ﴿And the last of us﴾ refers to those who come after us. ﴿And a sign from You﴾ as evidence of Your power and of my prophethood. ﴿And provide for us﴾ it (the table).

Allah said, responding to him: "Indeed, I am sending it down to you" (both readings, with and without shaddah, are recited). "So whoever among you disbelieves after that" (i.e., after its descent) "I will punish him with a punishment with which I will not punish anyone among the worlds."

So the angels brought it down from the sky, and upon it were seven loaves and seven fish. They ate from it until they were satisfied. This is related from Ibn ʿAbbas. And in a hadith: the table (al-Ma'idah) was sent down from the sky as bread and meat. They were commanded not to betray (the command) and not to store up food for the next day, but they betrayed and stored, so they were transformed into apes and swine.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 5, verse 116:

﴿And﴾ mention ﴿when Allah said﴾, that is, He will say ﴿to Jesus﴾ on the Day of Resurrection, rebuking his people: ﴿"O Jesus, son of Mary, did you say to the people, 'Take me and my mother as two gods besides Allah?'"﴾ He ﴿said﴾, and he was trembling: ﴿"Glory be to You"﴾, exalting You above what is unbecoming to You of partners and other things, ﴿"it is not for me to say what I have no right to say"﴾. The predicate of "laysa" (is not) is "li" (for me), where the "li" is for clarification. ﴿"If I had said it, You would have known it. You know what is in my soul, and I do not know what is in Your soul"﴾, that is, what You keep hidden of Your knowledge.

﴿I did not say to them except what You commanded me, namely: "Worship Allah, my Lord and your Lord." And I was a witness over them​**​** as a watcher, preventing them from what they say, ​for as long as I was among them. But when You caused me to die​ (took me up to the sky)​, You were the Watcher over them, the Guardian of their deeds. And You are over all things​ (of what I said to them, what they said after me, and other things) a Witness​, one who observes and knows it.﴾

﴿If You punish them﴾, that is, those among them who persisted in disbelief, ﴿then they are Your servants﴾, and You are their Owner, disposing of them as You wish, with no one to object to You; ﴿and if You forgive them﴾, that is, those among them who believed, ﴿then You are the Mighty﴾ over His command, ﴿the Wise﴾ in His creation.

﴿Allah will say, "This is"﴾ i.e., the Day of Resurrection, ﴿a Day on which the truthful will benefit from their truthfulness﴾ in the world, like ʿIsa, ﴿for it is the Day of Recompense. And the liars will not benefit from their truthfulness in it,﴾ like the disbelievers, ﴿because they believe at the sight of the punishment.﴾ ﴿For them are gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein forever. Allah is pleased with them﴾ for their obedience to Him, ﴿and they are pleased with Him﴾ for His reward. ﴿That is the great triumph.﴾ And the liars will not benefit from their truthfulness in it, like the disbelievers, because they believe at the sight of the punishment.

To Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth: the treasuries of rain, plants, provision and other things, ﴿and whatever is in them﴾. He used "má" (what) rather than "man" (who) for them as a predominance of the non-rational (ghayr al-'aql), ﴿and He is over all things Competent﴾. Among this is rewarding the truthful and punishing the liar. The Essence itself is excepted [from His power], so He is not capable of it.
